layer_vocabulary.notes: rules (the Decision layer): the policy engine — builtin Python handlers, cel_policy (CEL expressions), and custom Python policies returning ALLOW/ASK/DENY or abstaining (None, documented as equivalent to ALLOW for aggregation); evaluated at request / tool_call / tool_result / response events, levels in session -> agent -> server order, DENY short-circuits, any-DENY blocks else any-ASK pauses else the action proceeds; verdicts are stateful (session_state, labels, usage/cost context). approval (the Approval layer): the ASK verdict pauses the action until a user approves (approved -> ALLOW, refused -> DENY); state_updates are withheld on ASK pending approval; cost policies remember soft-threshold approvals per session / per user-day / per user-period; two always-on guards (ask_on_add_policy, ask_on_scheduled_task_change) cannot be removed. sandbox (part of the Effect layer — OS-level confinement): bubblewrap mandatory on Linux for native wrappers and the pi harness, seatbelt on macOS, L7 egress proxy, Windows Job Object degraded mode (no filesystem/network isolation); enforce_sandbox policy forces sandbox_type/allow_network/write_paths (incl. copy-on-write)/read_paths at agent start; agent CLIs spawn with a deny-by-default environment; cloud sandboxes (Modal, Daytona, etc.) per session. effect (the Effect layer — observed outcome): tool_result and response policy phases observe outcomes and assistant text (post-tool policies cannot undo an action); DENY reasons are logged; no Effect measurement exists — E1/E2 are applicable by design against the sandbox containment, unrun.

measurement_route_evidence: No documented check/evaluate/test decision entrypoint in the CLI or REST surfaces consulted (DOC-scope; no binary inspected), but ALLOW/ASK/DENY semantics, aggregation, stacking order, PolicyEvent/PolicyResponse schemas, and builtin parameters are documented precisely enough to evaluate a named subset (deterministic builtins + CEL map-form, declared fresh-session state) — labelled evaluation, never interrogation. (INFERENCE on DOC+REPRO)

config_files: agent YAML: top-level policies: block in the Omnigent/agent config (type: function, handler, factory_params)

server config YAML passed via omnigent server -c config.yaml: policies: block in the function: {path, arguments} form, plus policy_modules: for custom policy registration; also manageable at runtime via the Settings page and REST /v1/policies
session level (not a file): policies added via chat (sys_add_policy tool, approval-gated), the web UI settings panel, or the session REST surface — current session only, not persistent
decision_verbs: abstain (None — documented as equivalent to ALLOW for aggregation)
policy_ingestion.defaults: No policy opinion (all abstain, or no policies configured) -> the action proceeds; abstain is documented as equivalent to ALLOW. The only always-on exceptions are two non-removable approval guards appended to every session: ask_on_add_policy and ask_on_scheduled_task_change. Framework mapping: a no-opinion outcome is NOT an explicit ALLOW decision and MUST serialize as unknown with layer attribution, never as allow (INV-005). Verdicts are stateful: a decision is a function of the event plus accumulated session_state, so an adapter must declare its assumed session state (fresh session is the honest default).
policy_ingestion.surface: YAML policies: blocks at three stacking levels (session / agent config / server-wide; evaluated in that order, all enforced simultaneously, DENY short-circuits). Each entry names a builtin or custom Python handler by dotted path (handler + factory_params, or function: {path, arguments} at server level), a cel_policy builtin carrying a CEL expression, or a custom Python policy registered via policy_modules + POLICY_REGISTRY. Plain-language assembly in chat outputs one of these forms and is itself approval-gated. Events: request / tool_call / tool_result / response, carrying a documented PolicyEvent schema; responses follow the documented PolicyResponse schema.

spike_answers.a_native_oracle: NO (DOC-scope). No check/evaluate/test/dry-run policy entrypoint appears in any primary surface consulted: the README's full CLI surface (run, server, host, start, stop, attach, login, setup, config, sandbox, upgrade, uninstall, per-harness launchers) has no policy-decision command, and the documented REST surface is runtime management only (POST|GET|PATCH|DELETE /v1/policies; GET /v1/policy-registry lists the registry with parameter schemas) — no evaluate/test endpoint. Two structural bars to a vendor-confirmed route regardless: verdicts are stateful (a function of the event plus accumulated session_state, so (policy, command) -> verdict is undefined without a declared session state), and several builtins are LLM evaluators (stochastic). Executing vendor handler code under our own driver would still be reconstructed, never vendor-confirmed. Caveat: no binary was installed or inspected in this spike, so this NO is documentary, not binary-verified.
spike_answers.b_documented_semantics: YES, for a named subset. Documented precisely and consistently across two primary surfaces (omnigent.ai policy docs + repo docs/POLICIES.md): verdict vocabulary ALLOW/ASK/DENY + abstain (None == ALLOW for aggregation); aggregation (any DENY blocks, else any ASK pauses, else proceed; DENY short-circuits; declaration order within a level); stacking (session -> agent -> server, all enforced simultaneously); the PolicyEvent schema (request/tool_call/tool_result/response; data{name, arguments}; context{actor, usage, model, harness, labels}; session_state) and PolicyResponse schema (result, reason, data replacement, state_updates withheld on ASK, set_labels); parameters of the catalogue-relevant builtins (github_policy force-push/destructive defaults, ask_on_os_tools, enforce_sandbox, cost thresholds, worktree_guard, read_only_os). Ceilings: blast_radius classification table unpublished; CEL return contract documented inconsistently (map-form vs boolean-true-to-deny; two handler paths); LLM-evaluator policies stochastic and partly fail-open; per-domain shell parsers documented only for github_policy / block_working_dir_changes, no general compound-command semantics; verdicts stateful, so evaluations must declare assumed session state.
